title: Field of rational functions in one indeterminate
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $T$ an indeterminate, with polynomial ring $K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The *field of rational functions* $K(T)$ is the field of fractions of $K[T]$: its elements are the fractions $P/Q$ with $P,Q\in K[T]$, $Q
eq0$, where $P/Q=P'/Q'$ if and only if $PQ'=P'Q$, with $P/Q+P'/Q'=(PQ'+P'Q)/(QQ')$ and $(P/Q)(P'/Q')=(PP')/(QQ')$; $K[T]$ is the subring of the fractions $P/1$, and $K\subset K[T]$ the constants. Every nonzero $R\in K(T)$ has a unique *reduced presentation* $R=N/D$ with $N,D\in K[T]$, $D$ monic and $\gcd(N,D)=1$ (from any presentation $P/Q$, divide $P$ and $Q$ by $\gcd(P,Q)$ and by the leading coefficient of the quotient of $Q$). For $a\in K$, $R$ is *regular at $a$* if $D(a)
eq0$ in its reduced presentation, and its *value* is then $R(a)=N(a)/D(a)\in K$. For $S\in K(T)$ transcendental over $K$, *substitution of $S$ for $T$* is the $K$-algebra homomorphism $K(T)	o K(T)$, $R=P/Q\mapsto R(S)=P(S)/Q(S)$, where $P(S)$ is the image of $P$ under the $K$-algebra homomorphism $K[T]	o K(T)$ sending $T$ to $S$; it is well defined because that homomorphism is injective ($S$ is transcendental), so $Q(S)
eq0$ for $Q
eq0$, and it is the identity on $K$. For $c\in K^	imes$, $S=cT^{-1}$ is transcendental over $K$ ($T=cS^{-1}$ is rational in $S$, so if $S$ were algebraic over $K$ then so would be $T$), and substituting $cT^{-1}$ twice gives back $R$; so $R\mapsto R(cT^{-1})$ is an involutive automorphism of $K(T)$. For a polynomial $P\in K[T]$ and $S\in K(T)$, $P(S)$ is the usual evaluation of $P$ at $S$.
